start.name: Ras Shukheir facility (oil/gas station area, N of Hurghada), Red Sea Governorate, Egypt
start.coord_basis: Pinned to the exact start coordinate of the already-applied, GulfPub-sourced P8016 'Ras Shukheir-Suez Trunkline Gas Pipeline' route in the routes repo (data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P8016.geojson) -- P8034 is the middle piece of a three-segment corridor with P8016 (Ras Shukheir->Suez, mapped 'high' accuracy) to the north and P6034 (Hurghada->Safaga, mapped) to the south, per the brief, so its Ras Shukheir end is pinned to coincide exactly with P8016's Ras Shukheir end rather than an independently re-geocoded point. Independently corroborated (not fabricated): Wikipedia's 'Ras Shokeir' article places the named oil/gas facility area at 28.131414N 33.248477E (~3.8 km away); a maritime vessel-tracking database entry for Ras Shukheir used in a prior batch pass (VesselFinder, 28.1339N 33.2814E) sits <1 km from this point.

end.name: Hurghada (gas receiving point, matches applied P6034 Hurghada-Safaga line's Hurghada end), Red Sea Governorate, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Pinned to the exact start coordinate of the already-applied P6034 'Hurghada-Safaga Gas Pipeline' route in the routes repo (data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P6034.geojson), for the same corridor-continuity reason as the Ras Shukheir end (P8034 hands off to P6034 at Hurghada). Independently corroborated: Wikipedia gives Hurghada city-center coordinates as 27.25778N 33.81167E, ~1.9 km from this point -- consistent with a gas-network node on the northern/inland edge of the city rather than the beachfront center.

corridor_desc: Overland corridor down the Gulf of Suez / Red Sea coast between Ras Shukheir and Hurghada -- the middle of a three-segment chain (P8016 north of Ras Shukheir, P8034 the middle piece, P6034 south of Hurghada to Safaga). No independent route-geometry source (GulfPub, EIA, map) was found specifically for this middle segment; the corridor is presumed to run along the coastal road/pipeline right-of-way used by the two adjoining mapped segments, consistent with the sheet's 127 km length (vs. ~103 km geodesic between the pinned endpoints -- a plausible coastal-routing overhead).

facts.source: EGAS Annual Report 2018 (per sheet's existing Length/Diameter [ref]); no additional trade-press hit found this pass specifically naming this segment (searches surfaced only the adjoining P8016/P6034 segments and the general Suez-Sinai gas network).

notes: Both endpoints are anchored to the exact coordinates already used by the routes repo for the two adjoining, already-mapped GEM pipelines (P8016 Ras Shukheir-Suez to the north, P6034 Hurghada-Safaga to the south) per the brief's instruction to 'pin the two endpoint stations.' Each pinned point was independently cross-checked against a public gazetteer/encyclopedia coordinate for the named place (Wikipedia) and landed within 2-4 km, which is normal for a settlement-level place name vs. a specific pipeline valve/station location, and is not itself evidence the two points are the same infrastructure -- only that the pin is in the right named place. No trade-press or EIA document specifically describing the middle 'Ras Shukeir-Hurghada' segment by name was found this pass (EGAS Annual Report 2018's pipeline grid table did not extract as searchable text -- likely embedded as a graphic; consistent with earlier passes in this batch also failing to text-search that table). RouteAccuracy should stay at most 'low' or 'very low (straight line/schematic)' given no source directly traces the middle segment's path.

Direct row comparison in data/GGIT_gas_snapshot_20260804.csv (header=2) confirms: identical PipelineName ('Trans Gulf Gas Pipeline'), identical Status (operating), identical LengthKnown (75.0 km), identical Capacity (110.0 MMcf/d) and CapacityUnits, identical StartLocation text ('Petreco Plant'), and matching EndPrefecture/District ('Ras Baker Transmissin Station' on P8013 vs 'Ras Bakr' on P8035 -- clearly the same name, one row's spelling corrected by the CB research pass, the other not). The only difference is Diameter (P8013 blank, P8035 '12in') and StartState/Province wording ('Sinia' vs 'South Sinia') / EndState/Province ('Gulf of Suez' vs 'Red Sea') -- both are the same governorate referenced two different ways, not conflicting facts. P8013 already has an APPLIED route in the routes repo (RouteType='Mapped route (at any accuracy)', RouteAccuracy='very low (straight line/schematic)', RouteCreator='CB', per the 2026-07-30 retry-pass apply referenced in staged_resolutions.json and the egypt.md country notes). RECOMMENDATION: do not create a second independent route candidate for P8035 -- flag it for a human duplicate-adjudication decision (likely retire/merge P8035 into P8013, carrying over P8035's Diameter value which P8013 is missing) rather than mapping it as a second real pipeline. I reproduced P8013's already-researched endpoints above only so the duplicate claim is fully documented, not as newly verified geocoding for P8035 itself.

start.name: El-Tena East valve room (GASCO Abr Sinai pipeline take-off point), El Tina plain, Egypt (Port Said/Ismailia border area, west bank of the El Sheikh Gaber Canal corridor)
start.coord_basis: EIB-published GASCO 'Abr Sinai Onshore Gas Pipeline' Environmental Impact Assessment (PETROSAFE, Nov 2007), Section 3.1: 'The route of pipeline starts from the existed valve room of El-Tena East site (long. 31 01'27.74" lat. 32 20'39.3")... heads south... then turn east crossing El-Qantar - Port Foad Road, and continue parallel to El-Sheikh Gaber Canal'. NOTE: the source document's own 'long.'/'lat.' column labels are transposed at every coordinate it gives (all four points I extracted have 'long.'=~31 deg and 'lat.'=~32-34 deg, which is backwards for Sinai geography where latitude runs ~30-31N and longitude ~32-34E) -- I have corrected for this systematic swap in the value reported here (lat=31.024372N, lon=32.344250E), and it is internally consistent: this puts the point on the El Tina plain just south of the Port Said/El Qantara road crossing described in the same sentence.

end.name: Roman (Romani/Rummana) compressing station, North Sinai Governorate, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Same EIA, Section 3.1: pipeline runs '...in the back area of Roman village to be connected to Roman compressing station (long. 31 01'23.9" lat. 32 40'06.3") (End point of Loop 1, from KM 0.00 to KM 33.00)' -- same long./lat. swap corrected as above (lat=31.023306N, lon=32.668417E). Independently corroborated: Wikidata's 'Romani' entry (a real, distinct town in North Sinai, alt. name Rumani) gives 31 1'N, 32 42'E (~31.017N, 32.7E) -- 3.4 km from the corrected EIA point, i.e. the EIA's compressing station sits just west of Romani town, which is exactly what 'in the back area of Roman village' implies.

corridor_desc: From the El-Tena East valve room, south ~400 m then east across the El-Qantara-Port Fouad road, then east along the west bank of the El-Sheikh Gaber Canal (parallel to the HV transmission towers), reaching the El-Qantara-El-Arish road, then east along the north side of that road through the back of Roman/Romani village to the Roman compressing station. Per the EIA this segment ('Loop 1') runs from chainage KM 0.00 to KM 33.00 (~33 km) as the second, parallel 36in line alongside an already-existing pipeline on (per the EIA) essentially the same alignment.

facts.source: Sheet: EGAS Annual Report 2018. EIA: GASCO began construction of a parallel/duplicate 36in, 111 km 'Abr Sinai' pipeline (this El-Tena East-Roman segment plus the Bair El-Abd-Arish segment, P8044) 01-Nov-2007 to 31-Jul-2009 per the EIA's own project time schedule (Table 3.2).

flags: length-mismatch:sheet gives 55.0 km for El-Tena East-Roman, but the EIA's own chainage for this exact segment (Loop 1, 'from KM 0.00 to KM 33.00') is 33 km, not 55 -- a ~67% difference that is too large to be rounding. The endpoints below are still the best-sourced, checkable anchors for the named places regardless of which alignment/length GEM's 55 km figure reflects (it may describe the original single, pre-2007 line on a longer alignment, or simply be a table transcription issue in the 2018 EGAS source) -- flagging for researcher review rather than adjudicating.

coord-label-swap-corrected:source PDF's own long./lat. labels are transposed for every coordinate in the document (see coord_basis) -- corrected values are reported above, not the document's raw labels.
notes: Strong, well-sourced endpoints from a primary EIB project EIA (not GEM, not abarrelfull), independently cross-checked by matching the 'Roman' endpoint to the real town of Romani/Rummana (Wikidata) 3.4 km away, and by the El-Tena East point's narrative fitting known geography (El Tina plain, El-Qantara-Port Fouad road, El-Sheikh Gaber Canal). The one open issue is the length mismatch flagged above -- worth a follow-up check of the EGAS 2018 report's actual pipeline-grid table (its text did not extract cleanly from the PDF this pass, consistent with prior passes in this batch also failing to text-search that table; it may need OCR to resolve which figure -- 33 or 55 km -- EGAS itself reports for this named segment).

end.name: El-Areish industrial-area end point (Abr Sinai duplication-loop terminus), near El Arish, North Sinai Governorate, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Same EIA: '...heads to the East direction to El-Areish parallel to the existed 36" pipeline...then crossing the Airport road heads to End point At El-Areish (long. 31 05'43.9" lat. 33 50'36.1") with a total distance of 78 KM End of Loop 2' -- swap corrected (lat=31.095528N, lon=33.843361E). This sits ~4.1 km SSE of El Arish city center (Wikipedia gives El Arish at approx. 31.13N, 33.80E), consistent with the EIA's own description of an 'El-Areish Industrial area' delivery point on the city's edge rather than downtown.

corridor_desc: From the Bair El-Abd valve room, east parallel to (and ~10 m from) the existing 36in Abr Sinai pipeline and the El-Qantara-El-Arish road, crossing a paved road at El-Midan village, then continuing along the same road corridor, crossing the airport road, to the El-Areish industrial-area end point on the southeastern edge of El Arish. Per the EIA this segment ('Loop 2') runs a total of ~78 km, closely matching the sheet's 75.0 km.

facts.source: Sheet: EGAS Annual Report 2018. EIA: same 2007-2009 duplication project as P8041 (Table 3.2 time schedule, 'Duplication of Abr Sinai P/L 36" 111KM', 01-Nov-2007 to 31-Jul-2009).

not-duplicate-of:P3659 -- checked per brief instruction. P3659 'Port Said-Arish Gas Pipeline' (235 km, 36/42in, El Gamil->El Arish, RouteAccuracy='high') is a DIFFERENT, parallel trunk approaching Arish via the direct Port Said/El Gamil coastal corridor, not via El Qantara/El Tina/Bair El-Abd. Oil & Gas Journal's account of GASCO's Sinai gas-supply build-out independently describes multiple distinct routes into the Arish area ('Abr Sinai' duplication project covered here, plus a separate route via Oyoun Mousa-El Arish-Rafah continuing to Sharm El-Sheikh -- see P8045), consistent with two genuinely separate, non-duplicate pipelines both terminating near El Arish.
notes: Endpoints are well-sourced from the same primary EIB EIA used for P8041, with the same long./lat.-label correction applied and independently cross-checked against Wikipedia coordinates for Bir al-Abd and El Arish. Length (75 km sheet vs. 78 km EIA) is a close, unremarkable match -- no flag needed there (unlike P8041's larger discrepancy). Diameter (36in) matches exactly. Checked the brief's specific concern about identity confusion with GEM's already-mapped P3659 (Port Said-Arish, high-accuracy route) and found no evidence they are the same pipeline -- they are two genuinely separate corridors into the Arish area, per trade press.

end.name: Sharm El-Sheikh Thermal Power Plant, Qesm Sharm Ash Sheikh, South Sinai Governorate, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Global Energy Observatory (GEO) facility record 'Sharm El-Sheikh Thermal Power Plant Egypt' (geoid/5352) -- an independent, non-GEM legacy energy-infrastructure database (same database class used for a Suez-area endpoint in a prior pass of this batch). Chosen as the end point because Oil & Gas Journal's 2006/2007 report on this exact pipeline ('Taba/Sharm El-Sheikh pipeline, 220 km of 20in...will carry up to 6 MMcfd to serve the cities on the route, hotels and tourist villages, in addition to power stations in Taba, Noweba, Dahab and Sharm El-Sheikh') names power stations along the route as delivery points, and this is the only power station identifiable by name and location in Sharm El-Sheikh itself. Second independent source (power-technology.com plant profile) corroborates the plant's existence/location description ('South Sinai, Egypt') but does not itself give coordinates or confirm gas as a fuel (it lists light fuel oil primary / hydrogen backup, not gas -- see flag below).

corridor_desc: Down the Gulf of Aqaba coast from Taba, past Nuweiba and Dahab (both named as served towns/power-station sites by the OGJ source), to Sharm El-Sheikh -- essentially following the coastal highway. No source gives interior waypoints for Nuweiba or Dahab; only the two named endpoints are anchored here, consistent with the sheet's 206 km length (OGJ gives 220 km for the same pipeline -- a close, unremarkable match given it is describing the same 2006-built, 20in line).

facts.source: Sheet: EGAS Annual Report 2018 / EGO&G May-2007 newspaper (per sheet's existing [ref]s). Oil & Gas Journal: pipeline built 2006, 'went on line in early 2007', 220 km of 20in pipe, ~6 MMcfd capacity, cost ~L.E. 511 million -- independently corroborates the sheet's length, diameter, and 2007 start year for the same named pipeline.

flags: fuel-mismatch-unresolved:the power-technology.com profile for the Sharm El-Sheikh Thermal Power Plant lists its fuel as light fuel oil (primary) with hydrogen as backup, not natural gas -- odd given OGJ's explicit statement that this pipeline supplies gas to a Sharm El-Sheikh power station. Not resolved this pass; flagging rather than assuming either source is wrong. Possible explanations not verified: the plant's fuel mix changed since the 2006/2007 build, 'Hydrogen' in the profile is a data error/mistranslation, or the pipeline serves a different Sharm El-Sheikh facility than the one GEO/power-technology profile.
notes: Both endpoints are well-sourced: Taba is pinned to the same point GEM already uses for the adjoining Arab Gas Pipeline segment (independently corroborated via Wikipedia, ~250 m match), and Sharm El-Sheikh is anchored to a named, independently-databased power station (Global Energy Observatory) that Oil & Gas Journal explicitly names as one of this pipeline's delivery points. The OGJ trade-press article is a strong, independent, non-GEM, non-abarrelfull source that directly describes this exact pipeline by route (Taba-Sharm El-Sheikh), length (220 km vs sheet's 206), diameter (20in, matches exactly), capacity, cost, and 2007 commissioning -- satisfying the 2+ independent source bar together with the sheet's existing EGAS/newspaper refs. One open flag: the power plant's documented fuel type doesn't obviously match a gas-fed facility (see flags) -- worth a follow-up check, but does not undermine the location anchor itself since OGJ names the town/power-station relationship, not this specific database's fuel listing.
